Folks — I created two worked examples and a simple pricing calc. See table below (pasted) and attached spreadsheet for line-by-line math. Attachment: pricing_calc.xlsx

Example A — one production day
- Short calls: 10,000 calls * (150 in + 60 out) = 2,100,000 tokens
- Rounding: short-call quantum = 64 tokens — we round each call up to the nearest 64. Effective billed tokens for short calls = 10,000 * ceil(210/64)*64 = 10,000 * 256 = 2,560,000 tokens
- Nightly batch: 1,200 prompts * (6,200 in + 1,800 out) = 9,600,000 tokens
- Batch quantum: enterprise long-job quantum = 1024 tokens for billing efficiency. Billed tokens = ceil(9,600,000 / 1024) * 1024 = 9,600,000 (already multiple)
- Prefix caching: if prefix (200 tokens) is pinned as a reusable KV prefix across the batch, we credit prefix reuse. For the batch that reduces billed tokens by 1,200 * 200 = 240,000 tokens (policy: credit applied as negative line item).
- Day total billed tokens = 2,560,000 + 9,600,000 - 240,000 = 11,920,000 tokens

Example B — weekly enrichment (6,000 prompts)
- Raw tokens = 6,000 * (6,200 + 1,800) = 50,400,000 tokens
- Billed (1k quantum) = 50,400,000 (no extra round)
- Prefix credit = 6,000 * 200 = 1,200,000 credit
- Total = 49,200,000 tokens

Pricing/discount notes:
- Base per-token price X applies to billed tokens above; for pilots we can apply a 10% effective pilot discount on the long-job volume band (>10M tokens/day) or structure a committed seat + token blend.
- Rounding creates a notable delta for high-volume short calls; for Acme we recommend enabling short-call aggregation (prefix batching) or switching short calls to a micro-batched endpoint that reduces per-call quantum to 1 token (costlier latency tradeoff).

See attached spreadsheet for the exact math and a mock invoice. Vanessa
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — this aligns with policy. Two operational/legal points we should surface to Acme in the reply:

1) Prefix crediting: we can offer a KV-prefix reuse credit for jobs that are single-traceable batch runs (same prompt template + pinned metadata). We require the customer to enable prefix pinning and we audit one sample run per quarter. The credit shows as a negative line on invoices.

2) Rounding/aggregation exceptions: for pilots we can temporarily override short-call quantum to 1 token for up to 90 days or until the committed volume threshold is reached (proposal: 90-day pilot with 10% pilot discount on long-job billed tokens and short-call quantum override). Any permanent change must be part of an enterprise contract addendum.

Jordan — commercial: does 10% plus quantum override align with a standard pilot concession? If not, suggest a counter.

Irene
Head of Contracts & Pricing Policy, Redwood Inference

Draft reply to Jamie (send from Soojin):

Hi Jamie — thanks for the usage detail, that helps. Short answer: you are billed per-token but we apply quanta and have explicit prefix-crediting for batch workloads. Attached is an example invoice and a worked calculation for your day and weekly enrichment. Below are the key points and a pilot proposal we can offer Acme: 

- Metering: per-token metering, default rounding quanta: short calls = 64 tokens; long streaming/batch = 1024 tokens. We can set these quanta for pilots.
- Prefix reuse credit: eligible when prefix is pinned and batch job audited — we will credit repeated prefix tokens as a negative invoice line.
- Pilot commercial: 90-day pilot, 10% discount on billed long-job tokens (volume band >10M/day), short-call quantum overridden to 1 token for the pilot window. After pilot, revert to defaults unless an enterprise commit is signed.

If that looks good we will send a formal pilot SOW and update the pricing spreadsheet with your estimated volumes to give a projected monthly cost.
